notes:
Charge & Coulomb's Law

  • Charge is quantised: $q = ne$, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}$ C. Charge is additive and conserved.
  • Coulomb's law: $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^2} = k\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^2}$, $k = 9\times10^9$ N m$^2$C$^{-2}$, $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$N$^{-1}$m$^{-2}$.
  • In a medium of dielectric constant $K$: $F_{medium} = F_{vacuum}/K$.
  • Superposition: net force is the vector sum of forces due to individual charges.

Electric Field

  • $\vec{E} = \vec{F}/q_0$; field of a point charge $E = kq/r^2$, directed away from a positive charge.
  • Field lines: start on +, end on −, never cross, denser where field is stronger, perpendicular to conductor surface.

Electric Dipole

  • Dipole moment $p = q(2a)$, direction − to +.
  • Axial (end-on) field: $E_{axial} = \dfrac{2kp}{r^3}$ (for $r \gg a$).
  • Equatorial (broadside-on) field: $E_{eq} = \dfrac{kp}{r^3}$, opposite direction to $\vec{p}$.
  • Torque in uniform field: $\tau = pE\sin\theta = \vec{p}\times\vec{E}$; potential energy $U = -pE\cos\theta$; stable equilibrium at $\theta=0$, unstable at $\theta=180^\circ$.

Continuous Charge Distributions

  • Linear density $\lambda = q/l$, surface density $\sigma = q/A$, volume density $\rho = q/V$.

Gauss's Law & Applications

SourceField
Infinite line charge$E = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r}$
Infinite plane sheet$E = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$
Charged conductor surface$E = \dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}$
Uniformly charged sphere ($r>R$)$E = \dfrac{kq}{r^2}$
Uniformly charged sphere ($r$E = \dfrac{kqr}{R^3}$
Conducting/hollow sphere ($r$E = 0$
  • Electric flux $\phi = \oint\vec{E}\cdot d\vec{A} = q_{enc}/\varepsilon_0$ — depends only on enclosed charge, not on shape/size of the Gaussian surface or charges outside.

Exam tip

KCET usually sets 2–3 questions from this chapter — expect one Coulomb's law/superposition numerical, one dipole field/torque question, and one Gauss's law application (sheet, sphere or line charge). Memorise the table above cold.

questions.q: Two point charges 2 $\mu$C and 8 $\mu$C are separated by 30 cm in air. The electrostatic force between them is nearly
questions.explanation: $F = k\dfrac{q_1q_2}{r^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times2\times10^{-6}\times8\times10^{-6}}{0.09} = \dfrac{0.144}{0.09} = 1.6\,\text{N}$.

questions.q: Two identical point charges each of magnitude $q$ are placed 20 cm apart in vacuum and the force between them is $F$. If they are now placed in a medium of dielectric constant 5 at the same separation, the new force is
questions.explanation: Force in a medium reduces by the dielectric constant: $F_{medium} = F/K = F/5$.

questions.q: A charge of $+4\,\mu$C experiences a force of 0.8 N at a point in an electric field. The magnitude of the electric field at that point is
The electric field due to a point charge $q$ at a distance $r$ is $E$. At what distance from the charge will the field be $E/9$?
questions.explanation: $E \propto 1/r^2$, so field reduces to $1/9$ when distance triples: $r' = 3r$.

questions.q: An electric dipole of dipole moment $p$ is placed in a uniform electric field $E$ with its axis making $60^\circ$ with the field. The torque on it is
questions.explanation: $\tau = pE\sin\theta = pE\sin60^\circ = pE\sqrt3/2$.

questions.q: The electric field due to a short dipole at a point on its axial line at distance $r$ (with $r \gg$ dipole length) is $E$. The field at the same distance on the equatorial line is
questions.explanation: $E_{axial} = 2kp/r^3$ and $E_{eq} = kp/r^3$, so $E_{eq} = E_{axial}/2$.

questions.q: A dipole of moment $2\times10^{-8}$ C m is placed in a uniform field of $5\times10^4$ N/C, initially aligned along the field. The work done to rotate it through $180^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: $W = U(180^\circ)-U(0^\circ) = pE - (-pE) = 2pE = 2\times2\times10^{-8}\times5\times10^4 = 2\times10^{-3}$ J.

questions.q: According to Gauss's law, the electric flux through a closed surface depends on
options: charges both inside and outside the surface
questions.explanation: Gauss's law states $\phi = q_{enc}/\varepsilon_0$, independent of the surface's shape or size and unaffected by charges outside it.

questions.q: A point charge of 8.85 $\mu$C is placed at the centre of a cube of side 1 m. The electric flux through one face of the cube is
questions.explanation: Total flux $= q/\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-6}/8.85\times10^{-12} = 1\times10^6$; by symmetry one of 6 faces gets $1/6$ of it $= 1.67\times10^5$ N m$^2$/C.

questions.q: The electric field just outside the surface of a charged conductor with surface charge density $\sigma$ is
questions.explanation: For a conductor surface, $E = \sigma/\varepsilon_0$ (twice the field of an isolated infinite sheet of the same $\sigma$).

questions.q: Inside a uniformly charged hollow conducting sphere, the electric field is
options: equal to the field at the surface
inversely proportional to distance from centre
questions.explanation: All charge resides on the outer surface; a Gaussian surface inside encloses zero charge, so $E=0$ inside.

questions.q: Two infinite parallel plane sheets carry equal and opposite uniform surface charge densities $\sigma$. The electric field in the region between the plates is
questions.explanation: Fields from both sheets ($\sigma/2\varepsilon_0$ each) add up between the plates: total $= \sigma/\varepsilon_0$; outside the plates they cancel to zero.

questions.q: An infinite line charge of linear density $\lambda$ produces an electric field at perpendicular distance $r$ given by
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law with a cylindrical surface, $E(2\pi r l) = \lambda l/\varepsilon_0 \Rightarrow E = \lambda/(2\pi\varepsilon_0 r)$, falling as $1/r$ (not $1/r^2$).

questions.q: Three point charges $+q$, $+q$ and $-2q$ are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. The net charge enclosed relevant to Gauss's law for a sphere surrounding all three is
questions.explanation: Net enclosed charge $= q+q-2q = 0$, so total outward flux through the enclosing surface is zero (field need not be zero everywhere on it).

questions.q: Electric field lines around an isolated positive point charge are
questions.explanation: Field lines originate on positive charge and point radially outward in all directions.

questions.q: A charge $q$ is placed at the centre of a cube. If the charge is now moved to one corner of the cube (still inside), the total electric flux through the whole cube surface
questions.explanation: Total flux through a closed surface depends only on enclosed charge ($q/\varepsilon_0$), regardless of the charge's position inside.

questions.q: Two small identical conducting spheres carry charges $6\,\mu$C and $-2\,\mu$C. They are brought into contact and then separated. The charge on each sphere now is
questions.explanation: On contact, identical conductors share total charge equally: $(6+(-2))/2 = 2\,\mu$C each.

questions.q: A solid sphere of radius $R$ carries a total charge $Q$ uniformly distributed through its volume. The electric field at a distance $r = R/2$ from the centre is
questions.explanation: Inside a uniformly charged solid sphere, $E = kQr/R^3$. At $r=R/2$: $E = kQ(R/2)/R^3 = kQ/(2R^2)$.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric dipole moment is
questions.explanation: $p = q\times(2a)$, product of charge (C) and separation (m), so unit is C m.

questions.q: A point charge $+q$ is kept 10 cm from another point charge $-q$. The electric field at the midpoint of the line joining them is directed
options: perpendicular to the line joining charges
zero, since charges are equal and opposite
from $+q$ to $-q$, magnitude $8kq/r_0^2$ where $r_0$ is total separation
questions.explanation: At the midpoint, fields due to $+q$ (pointing away, toward $-q$) and $-q$ (pointing toward it, same direction) add up: each contributes $kq/(r_0/2)^2 = 4kq/r_0^2$, total $8kq/r_0^2$, directed from $+q$ towards $-q$.

questions.q: A body acquires a charge of $3.2\times10^{-18}$ C. The number of electrons it must have gained is
Which of the following is a correct property of electric charge?
options: charge can take any arbitrary (non-quantised) value
total charge of an isolated system remains conserved
charge is not conserved in an isolated system
questions.explanation: Charge is a conserved, quantised, additive scalar quantity; like charges repel, they do not attract.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a correct property of electric field lines?
options: they can form closed loops in an electrostatic field
they are perpendicular to the surface of a conductor
two field lines can never cross each other
they start on positive charges and end on negative charges
questions.explanation: In electrostatics, field lines never form closed loops since the electrostatic field is conservative; the other three statements are correct.

questions.q: Coulomb's law constant $k = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$ has the approximate value
questions.explanation: $k=1/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)\approx9\times10^9$ N m$^2$C$^{-2}$ in vacuum/air.

questions.q: The electrostatic force between two point charges is $F$. If the distance between them is halved, the new force is
questions.explanation: $F\propto1/r^2$; halving $r$ quadruples the force.

questions.q: Two equal point charges placed at two corners of a right angle exert forces $F$ each, mutually perpendicular, on a third charge kept at the right-angle vertex. The net force on the third charge is
questions.explanation: The resultant of two equal, mutually perpendicular vectors of magnitude $F$ is $\sqrt{F^2+F^2}=F\sqrt2$.

questions.q: Compared to the electric field of a point charge (which falls as $1/r^2$), the electric field of a short dipole at large distances falls as
questions.explanation: Both the axial ($2kp/r^3$) and equatorial ($kp/r^3$) dipole fields fall off as $1/r^3$, faster than a monopole's $1/r^2$.

questions.q: The torque on an electric dipole placed in a uniform electric field is maximum when the angle between the dipole moment and the field is
questions.explanation: $\tau=pE\sin\theta$ is maximum at $\theta=90^\circ$, where $\sin\theta=1$.

questions.q: An electric dipole placed in a uniform electric field is in stable equilibrium when the angle between $\vec p$ and $\vec E$ is
questions.explanation: $U=-pE\cos\theta$ is minimum (most stable) at $\theta=0^\circ$, when $\vec p$ is aligned with $\vec E$.

questions.q: An electric dipole is placed in a non-uniform electric field. It experiences
options: neither a net force nor a torque
only a net force, never a torque
both a net force and (in general) a torque
only a torque, never a net force
questions.explanation: In a non-uniform field the forces on the two ends of the dipole are unequal, producing a net force, and in general also a net torque (in a uniform field only a torque acts, with zero net force).

questions.q: The SI unit of surface charge density $\sigma$ is
questions.explanation: Surface charge density is charge per unit area, $\sigma=q/A$, with SI unit C m$^{-2}$.

questions.q: An infinite plane sheet has a uniform surface charge density $\sigma = 4\times10^{-6}$ C m$^{-2}$. The electric field near the sheet (in air) is approximately
questions.explanation: $E=\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}=\dfrac{4\times10^{-6}}{2\times8.85\times10^{-12}}\approx2.26\times10^5$ N/C.

questions.q: Two point charges $+9q$ and $+q$ are placed 40 cm apart. The distance from the $+9q$ charge, along the line joining them, at which the net electric field is zero is
questions.explanation: At the neutral point, distance $x$ from $9q$: $\dfrac{9q}{x^2}=\dfrac{q}{(40-x)^2} \Rightarrow 3(40-x)=x \Rightarrow x=30$ cm.

questions.q: In $\beta^-$ decay, a neutron converts into a proton, an electron, and an antineutrino. This process illustrates that electric charge is
options: conserved (total charge before = total charge after)
questions.explanation: The neutron (charge 0) becomes a proton ($+e$) and an electron ($-e$); the total charge before and after remains zero, illustrating conservation of charge.

questions.q: The net electric field at a point due to a group of point charges is obtained by
options: scalar addition of the magnitudes of individual fields
vector addition of the fields due to each charge, treating others as absent
questions.explanation: By the superposition principle, the resultant field is the vector sum of the fields each charge would independently produce at that point.

questions.q: A rod of length 20 cm carries a uniformly distributed charge of 4 $\mu$C. Its linear charge density is
At a certain point, the electric field due to charge A alone is 3 N/C along the x-axis, and due to charge B alone is 4 N/C along the y-axis. The resultant electric field at that point has magnitude
questions.explanation: The two fields are perpendicular, so the resultant $=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$ N/C.

questions.q: The direction of the electric dipole moment vector $\vec p$ of a dipole is
options: from the negative charge to the positive charge
perpendicular to the line joining the charges
along the external electric field always
from the positive charge to the negative charge
questions.explanation: By convention, $\vec p$ points from the negative charge towards the positive charge, along the dipole axis.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding Gauss's law is INCORRECT?
options: It can be used to derive Coulomb's law
The flux through a closed surface depends on charges outside it as well
It is a consequence of the inverse-square nature of the electrostatic force
It is valid for any closed surface, regardless of its shape
questions.explanation: The flux through a closed surface depends only on the charge enclosed, not on any charges outside it — so this statement is incorrect; the other three are true.

questions.q: Two point charges $+q$ and $+4q$ are placed 30 cm apart. The point on the line joining them (between the charges) where the electric field is zero is at a distance from $+q$ of
questions.explanation: At distance $x$ from $+q$: $\dfrac{q}{x^2}=\dfrac{4q}{(30-x)^2} \Rightarrow 30-x=2x \Rightarrow x=10$ cm.
